newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds drift higher in lazy session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds drift higher in lazy session.

text.p: Most U.S. mortgage-backed securities floated modestly higher amid a sleepy Friday session, traders said.
"There haven't been any particularly large bid lists, there hasn't been a lot of activity (and) it has been remarkably quiet in terms of flows," said one Ginnie trader in New York.

Mortgages are "doing well here" as a function of a low volatility environment, he said. "Until we get greater insight as to what's going to happen in the (Treasury) market, you are not going to see the mortgage market do a whole lot," he said.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was up 4/32 at 100-27/32, yielding 115 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues rose 3/32 at 100-28/32 and 101-03/32, respectively.
Five-year Treasuries were up 3/32 at 6.71 percent, and 10-year notes were up 4/32 at 6.83 percent.
The mortgage market is "very tight," said Arthur Frank, vice president of mortgage research at HSBC Securities Inc.
He said investors are in pass-throughs for the dollar roll opportunities. With the April-May rolls, investors reaped profits while dealers had a very difficult month, he said.
"Near term, I would market weight mortgages as a sector," he said.
